Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:31: And it is written (Proverbs 10:22), "the blessing of the Lord makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it" — for sadness is drawn from the venom of Samael and the serpent that they injected into Adam and Eve, as it is written of Adam (Genesis 3:17), "in sadness (itzavon) shall you eat of it," and it is written (ibid. 16), "in sadness (etzev) shall you bear children,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:32: and through this the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah depart from him. And the proof is from Jacob, the chosen of the Patriarchs, from whom the Shechinah and the Holy Spirit were removed for twenty-two years, when Joseph was separated from him; and when he rejoiced at the news of him, it is written, "and the spirit of Jacob revived" — that the Holy Spirit rested upon him.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:33: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 117a), neither the Shechinah nor prophecy rests amid sadness, and so on. And so we find with Elisha and the sons of the prophets, as it is written (II Kings 3:15), "and it came to pass, when the minstrel played..." and it is written (I Samuel 10:5), "and before them a timbrel, a flute, and a lyre, and they are prophesying,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:34: and even in every act of divine service and praise, one must be in the utmost joy, as we find with Abaye (Berachot 30b), who was extremely cheerful and would say, "I am putting on tefillin" [with joy]; and likewise Rav Beruna, because he juxtaposed [the blessing of] redemption to prayer, laughter did not cease from his mouth that entire day:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:35: Hatred: through it one sins against his fellow, doing him every kind of harm. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 4), hatred of one's fellow creatures removes a person from the world; and behold, he thereby hates, as it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, for having created him, when in fact we are all children to the Lord our God; and he hates Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, from whom this person descended. And behold, all souls are bound up in the blessed Name and are a matter of supernal need, through which He is glorified — so how can you hate him?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:36: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 9b), the Second Temple had within it righteous men and great sages, and it was destroyed only for the sin of baseless hatred; and the end [of the exile] was not prolonged and hidden except for the reason of baseless hatred. And moreover, all other transgressions a person transgresses only at their appointed moment, but baseless hatred in the heart is constant, and every single moment one transgresses "you shall not hate," and nullifies the positive commandment (Leviticus 18:19), "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:37: and moreover, they said of this very commandment (Torat Kohanim, Parashat Kedoshim) that it is a great principle of the Torah, upon which the whole Torah depends; and Moses merited none of his virtues except that he loved Israel and was pained by their suffering, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Midrash Rabbah, Shemot ch. 1) regarding "and he saw their burdens," and regarding the verse (Exodus 32:32), "and now, if You will forgive their sin — and if not, erase me, I pray You"; and therefore he was equal in weight to all of Israel, as it is written (Isaiah 63:11), "and he remembered the days of old, Moses, his people":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:38: Envy is the cause that leads to hatred, and it is even more grave, for it rebels against the Holy One, blessed be He, as if to say: why did He bestow good upon my fellow more than upon me? And they said, of blessed memory (Avot ch. 4, mishnah 21), envy, desire, and [the pursuit of] honor remove a person from the world.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:39: Go and learn that all the earlier ones were punished only because of envy: for Cain, who spoke face to face with the blessed Name, was banished from the world, he and his offspring, because he was envious of Abel's twin sister, and through this he committed all those other transgressions; and the ten tribes were exiled to Assyria only for the sin that "his brothers envied him," and in the end were punished with the ten martyrs of the kingdom; and Jeroboam, before whom all the sages of his generation were as the grass of the field, was banished from the world through his envy of the kings of the House of David,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:40: and even Saul, the chosen of the Name, who as it were had not tasted the taste of sin, and had no flaw in his kingship, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 22b), was driven from his kingship and killed together with his three sons, and Nob, the city of the priests, was killed, and Israel were exiled at the hand of the Philistines, and the sanctuary of Shiloh was destroyed — and all this because he envied David regarding the matter of Goliath, so that the Holy Spirit departed from him and a spirit of confusion rested upon him:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:41: And the son of David will not come until envy is removed, as it is written (Isaiah 11:13), "Ephraim shall not envy Judah"; and moreover, even the angels on high fell from their holiness on account of this, as it is written in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chs. 13-14) regarding Samael, who was greater than the seraphim, who have only six wings, while he had twelve wings, and was uprooted from holiness on account of envy of man; and likewise the fallen ones, Uza and Azael, were banished from the world because they envied man:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:42: And whoever has envy, his bones rot; therefore a person should rightly be glad with his own portion, even if it is little, for is it not so with Hillel the Elder, and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, and Rabbi Yehuda bar Ila'i, and Rabbi Elazar ben Padat, and others like them:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:43: Covetousness is the father of impurity, for it leads to hatred and envy, and brings one to robbery, false oaths, and murder; and it is the tenth of the Ten Commandments, weighed as equal to all of them, for his eye is never satisfied with wealth, like the serpent, of which it is said (Isaiah 65:25), "and the serpent — dust shall be its food," and it is written (Proverbs 28:22), "a man with an evil eye hastens after wealth..."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:44: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said, desire removes a person from the world, for it distracts him from occupation with Torah and from fulfilling its commandments, and he is thereby a denier of Divine Providence, not believing that everything comes through the providence of the blessed Name, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 48b), whoever has bread in his basket and asks, "what shall I eat tomorrow?" — he is of those of little faith; and of him it is said (Zechariah 4), "for who has despised the day of small things?" — who caused it that the tables of the righteous will be plundered in the future to come? Their smallness of faith, which was in them:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:45: But trust — there is no trait as exalted as it, as it is written (Psalms 2:12), "happy are all who take refuge in Him," for he believes there is a God in the world who is able and who watches over all; and it is written (Jeremiah 17:7), "Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his trust" — and he is assured that his sustenance will not be lacking, as it is written (Psalms 55:23), "cast your burden upon the Lord, and He shall sustain you" — on condition that it be in truth and with his whole heart, without any doubt whatsoever; and moreover, when he trusts in the Lord, he will occupy himself with Torah and the commandments with his whole heart, without any distracting thought at all:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:46: The desire for pleasures is worse than all the traits mentioned above, for through being a glutton one comes to covetousness and robbery, to false oaths, to hatred of one's fellow creatures, and to envy, resembling Esau, of whom it is said (Genesis 25:30), "let me gulp down," and of him it is said (Proverbs 23:2), "and put a knife to your throat if you are a man given to appetite" — for through this he will eat carrion, torn animals, and every kind of forbidden food, and it is written (Ecclesiastes 6:7), "all of man's labor is for his mouth," and it is written (Proverbs 13:25), "but the belly of the wicked shall want,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:47: and it is written (Deuteronomy 32:15), "and Jeshurun grew fat and kicked" — "and abandoned the God who made him" — for it leads one to deny the blessed Name, as Scripture says (Proverbs 30:9), "lest I be full and deny, and say, who is the Lord?"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:48: And for all the other transgressions a minor is not punished, but the stubborn and rebellious son, who ate a tartemar of meat and drank half a log of wine, is stoned to death. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit 11a), the custom of the wicked is to eat meat and drink wine, and so on, and it is written (Isaiah 22:14), "surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die"; and Elijah, of blessed memory, said to Rabbi Yehuda (Berachot 29a), "Do not become drunk and you will not sin":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:49: But one who is content with the necessary minimum is called a tzaddik, as Scripture says (Proverbs 13:25), "the righteous one eats to satisfy his soul," and David said (Psalms 119:71), "it is good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn Your statutes," and Jacob asked for nothing more than (Genesis 28:20), "and give me bread to eat and clothing to wear," and it is written (ibid. 49:14), "Issachar is a large-boned donkey... and he bent his shoulder to bear" [the burden]:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:50: And they said, of blessed memory (Avot ch. 6, mishnah 4), such is the way of Torah: bread with salt shall you eat, and so on — if you do so, you are happy in this world and it is well with you in the World to Come; and they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 63a), the Torah endures only for one who puts himself to death over it. And they said, of blessed memory (Avot ch. 2, mishnah 7), more flesh, more worms.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:51: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit 11), a person should always regard himself as though a holy one dwelt in his innards, as it is said (Hosea 12:9), "a holy one is within you"; and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not merit to receive the Torah until he had fasted forty days and forty nights, and Elijah, of blessed memory, did not ascend on high until he had fasted forty days and forty nights, and Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Yishmael did not merit all that wisdom and prophecy in their ascent to the Pardes until they had fasted many days with every kind of self-affliction and abstinence; and Solomon, of whom it is said (I Kings 5:11), "and his fame was above all men," did not merit this until he had fasted forty days and forty nights, as they said regarding the enlarged "mem" of [the word] Mishlei (Proverbs), which is a "great mem":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:52: And in Sefer HaZohar (I, 11a), Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said to Rabbi Pinchas, when he saw that his body was covered with sores upon leaving the cave, "had you not seen me in this state, I would not have become like this."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:53: And in Parashat Terumah (141a): the bodies of the righteous, who did not draw themselves in this world after the pleasures of that kelipah — the spirit of impurity has no dominion over them at all, since, since they took pleasure in this world only in the pleasures of the commandments — the Sabbaths and the festivals — that spirit of impurity cannot rule over them at all, since they took no pleasure at all from what belongs to it; but if he did enjoy from what belongs to it on the weekdays, of him it is said (Malachi 2:3), "and I will spread dung upon your faces."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:54: And it was taught in the school of Elijah (Eliyahu Rabbah ch. 26): if a person has not merited Torah, let him seek mercy against excessive eating and drinking, that it not enter into his innards:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:55: <small>[Translation — Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said to Rabbi Pinchas, when he saw that his body was full of wounds upon leaving the cave, "had you not seen me thus, I would not be so." And in Parashat Terumah: the bodies of the righteous, who did not draw themselves in this world after the pleasures of that kelipah, the spirit of impurity has no dominion over them at all, since, as they took pleasure in this world only from the pleasure of the commandments, the Sabbaths and the festivals, that spirit of impurity cannot rule over them at all, since they took no pleasure at all from what belongs to it. But if he took pleasure from it on the weekdays, of him it is said, "and I will spread dung upon your faces."]</small>:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:56: Seeking authority and honor is exceedingly grave, for it brings a person to pride, which is the most grave of all; and through it he casts excessive dread upon the community not for the sake of Heaven, whose end is to be uprooted from the world, and whose offspring will never succeed after him at all,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:57: as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 101), and as we find with Jeroboam, the great sage, who, through seeking authority, was banished, he and his offspring, from this world, and has no share in the World to Come; and Saul, the chosen of the Lord, who as a one-year-old at the time of his kingship had not tasted the taste of sin, and hid himself among the baggage, fleeing from authority, yet in the end was caught in its net, and said (I Samuel 15:30), "honor me now before the elders of my people," and pursued it and lost his kingdom, and was killed, he and his three sons, as mentioned above concerning the trait of envy:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:58: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 4, mishnah 21), envy, desire, and [the pursuit of] honor remove a person from the world; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 55a), positions of leadership cut short and bury their holders, for they cause his heart to become haughty against his Maker, as it is written (Deuteronomy 17:20), "that his heart not become haughty... so that he may prolong his days over his kingdom."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:59: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 86b, Sanhedrin 7b), Rav, when he would go out to judge, would say, "of my own free will I go out to be killed," and so on. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Midrash Rabbah, Shemot ch. 27), "My son, if you have stood surety for your neighbor" (Proverbs 6:1) — Rav Huna interpreted this as referring to whoever is appointed as leader over the community; what is written after it? "You are snared by the words of your mouth, you are caught by the words of your mouth — do this now, my son, and save yourself"; and if not, of him it is written (ibid. 32), "whoever commits adultery lacks understanding, he destroys his own soul," and so on, and no mercy is shown to him in Gehinnom,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:60: The Holy One, blessed be He, says: I am holy, I am pious, and so on — if you have all these traits, accept authority upon yourself; but if not, do not accept it. And King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 131:1), "O Lord, my heart is not haughty... my soul is like a weaned child with its mother":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:61: Therefore flee from positions of authority to the very last degree, just as I have elaborated regarding the trait of pride, and as they said in Sefer HaZohar (III, 165a), happy is he who makes himself small in this world; and who is greater to us than Moses, the master of all Israel, who refused the Holy One, blessed be He, for seven days and did not wish [to accept the mission], and said (Exodus 4:13), "send, I pray, by the hand of whomever You will send," until it is said of him (ibid. 14), "and the anger of the Lord burned against Moses," and it left a mark upon him, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shemot Rabbah ch. 3), and afterward he consented, and in the end was punished on their account at the Waters of Meribah, and all his merits did not avail him.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:62: For whoever assumes authority over the community, even for the sake of Heaven, like Moses, is destined in the end to be punished, for he is a guarantor for all their deeds, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sifrei Devarim, piska 13) regarding "and I placed them at your head" — how much more so for orphans like us, who, God forbid, have no standing at all:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:63: Displaying one's good deeds to other people: you know what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yerushalmi Chagigah ch. 1) regarding that woman who was punished in Gehinnom because she would tell her friend, "today I fasted," and so on. And not only does he not receive reward, but he is even judged in Gehinnom, for he reveals thereby that his deeds are not at all for the sake of Heaven, and he is among those called "hypocritical abstainers," "the abstainers who wound" (Sotah 22b),
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 4:64: and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Eliyahu Rabbah, end of ch. 21), a person should always be one who fears Heaven in private, and let all his ways be for the sake of Heaven; and if a person can make all his ways for the sake of Heaven without revealing even one of them to other people, his reward is doubled and redoubled, since "the glory of God is to conceal a matter":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:1-3: Evil speech — our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Arachin 15b), it is worse than idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed, which are the most grave of all transgressions; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid.), whoever speaks evil speech is a denier of the fundamental principle, as it is written (Psalms 12:5), "who have said, with our tongue we shall prevail, our lips are with us — who is master over us?"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:4: Gossip-mongering kills three people, and is weighed as equal to bloodshed, and does not enter the Garden of Eden, as it is written (Psalms 15:1), "Who shall dwell in Your tent..." — "he who has not slandered with his tongue." And behold, Doeg the Edomite, the mightiest of the shepherds, the head of the Sanhedrin, was banished from the World to Come because of gossip-mongering, and was cut off in the midst of his days, and caused the killing of the men of Nob, the city of the priests, and the death of Saul and his sons and his household:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:5: Public humiliation, giving one's fellow a bad name, and glorifying oneself through another's shame — [those who do these] go down to Gehinnom and do not come up, and have no share in the World to Come; and they are included in "you shall not murder," as our Sages, of blessed memory, said, in the chapter "HaZahav" (Bava Metzia 58b): in the West [Eretz Yisrael], what were they most careful about? About [not causing a person's face to go from] red to white [i.e., public shame]:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:6: Mockery is one of the four classes that do not receive the presence of the Shechinah, and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avodah Zarah 18b), whoever mocks falls into Gehinnom; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 3, mishnah 2), even one who merely sits idle, this is [called] "a session of scoffers," as it is written (Psalms 1:1), "Happy is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked... nor sat in the session of scoffers," and immediately following, "but his delight is in the Torah of the Lord," and what is written after that? "and he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water..." "Not so the wicked..."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:7: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 6, mishnah 2), every day a heavenly voice goes forth and says, woe to the creatures for their disgrace of the Torah, for whoever does not occupy himself with Torah is called "rebuked" — meaning banned by Heaven. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 99b), "for he has scorned the word of the Lord" (Numbers 15:31), "that soul shall surely be cut off" — Rabbi Nechemiah says, this refers to anyone who is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not do so; and Rav said, whoever separates from words of Torah and occupies himself with idle talk, a fire consumes him; and whoever neglects himself from words of Torah falls into Gehinnom and is fed the coals of broom-bushes, as it is said (Job 30:4), "who pluck saltwort by the bushes"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 3, mishnah 5), whoever turns his heart to idleness thereby forfeits his own life, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:9), "only take heed to yourself..."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:8: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 7a), a person's judgment begins only with matters of Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 17:14), "the beginning of strife is like the letting out of water," and it is written (Joshua 1:8), "and you shall meditate on it day and night, for then you shall make your way successful, and then you shall prosper." And of every moment, hour, and day that a person is idle from words of Torah, it is said of him (Ecclesiastes 1:15), "and what is lacking cannot be counted,"
